text:
The Sabres have a few players playing very well and a team that isn't winning. Tage Thompson has been on a goal streak, Jack Quinn keeps scoring, and Jiri Kulich has found his touch at center (Buffalo Hockey Beat: "After early struggles, Sabres' Jiri Kulich becoming force at center"). And yet Buffalo is 11-11-4 and 3-6-1 over its last ten, getting 48% of the expected goals in that stretch.

The season numbers say this is a .500 team playing like one. Buffalo gets 49% of the expected goals overall and exactly half at five on five, and its scoring is right where its chances put it. The gap is in net: the Sabres have allowed about five more goals than the shots against them deserved. Friday's loss to Pittsburgh had the familiar shape, a second period Joe Yerdon of Bleacher Report called "brutal" and "like the ones we've seen before."

The bright spot is a line Lindy Ruff can lean on. Quinn, Noah Ostlund and Zach Benson have 59% of the expected goals and a 9-4 goal edge together, and Thompson with Peyton Krebs and Benson is 8-2. Rasmus Dahlin and Mattias Samuelsson carry nearly 300 minutes as the top pair and break even.

Our numbers give Buffalo a 27% chance at the playoffs. What we'd watch: whether the goaltending can at least match the shots, because the skaters are doing enough to stay in the race and not much more.
